newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil leaders set talks on Alagoas gov't crisis.
newsitem.headline: Brazil leaders set talks on Alagoas gov't crisis.

text.p: Brazilian government officials on Friday said a decision is expected this weekend on how to deal with a political crisis gripping the bankrupt state of Alagoas.
The governor of the northeastern state, facing impeachment, stepped down Thursday, the same day as striking police traded shots with troops outside the legislative assembly there.

Justice Minister Iris Rezende on Friday said President Fernando Henrique Cardoso would hold talks in Rio de Janeiro Saturday with Alagoas Vice Governor Manoel Barros, who now is in charge of the state government.

After a meeting with Cardozo and other political leaders, Rezende told reporters most of the participants had favored federal intervention in the state, where civil servants have not been paid in nine months.
"But the president decided he wanted to give the vice governor a chance first," the minister said. Federal intervention was a "last resort", he added.
On Thursday evening, presidential spokesman Sergio Amaral virtually ruled out federal intervention.
"If we had wanted to intervene, we would have done so a long time ago," Amaral said.

Federal intervention would have carry consequences well beyond the state itself, as it would effectively block progress of the federal government's sweeping reform program, which involves amending the Brazilian constitution.

The constitution cannot be amended during a period of intervention. Thus a federal move into Alagoas would freeze key pension and civil service reforms, and an extension of a $26 billion special budget fund, which are being considered in Congress.
